If you don't know what ME3 multiplayer is then here's a rundown:

ME3 multiplayer is a horde mode where you and up to 3 other players attempt to survive against 10 waves of increasingly challenging enemies of either Cerberus, Geth, Reapers, or Collectors. Some waves have objectives which must be completed before defeating the remaining enemies. Higher waves pit the team against more difficult enemies, so while the first few waves against Cerberus will be against Troopers, Centurions, and Nemesis, later waves will be filled with Phantoms, Dragoons, and Atlas mechs. Higher difficulties will require you to defeat more, higher tier enemies with increased stats. Platinum includes enemies from all factions except Collectors, unless you choose them as the primary faction.

Each player selects a character and loadout that they will play as during the match. What character you select determines which powers you'll have access to while the rest of your loadout consists of weapons, attachments, and equipment that modifies your character's stats or gives them extra equipment or abilities. Characters range from the basic biotic-wielding Human Adept, to the sword-carrying N7 Shadow infiltrator who deals devastating melee attacks from stealth, to the towering Geth Juggernaut soldier who cannot be sync killed and can drain shields from enemies with its heavy melee attack.

Multiplayer progression is entirely loot box based where you have to unlock characters and weapons by spending credits on packs in the store. Back when this game was new you could also spend real money but thankfully that feature has been disabled. It takes around 150 million credits to unlock everything, that being: all characters and their customization options, all level 10 weapons, all level 5 attachments, and all level 5 gear mods. You earn ~150k credits for a full extraction on the highest difficulty which takes ~30 minutes with an average team but can be completed much faster if you are speedrunning or specifically farming credits. That means it will take you ~500 hours to obtain everything if you only played on Platinum.

Luckily, you are on PC so you don't have to do that if you don't want to. You can completely skip the grind by using the developer console or cheat engine to give yourself credits to buy everything instantly (though this still takes a few hours of opening packs). To enable the dev console, download and install ME 3 Tweaks mod manager then input the following commands:

unlockallmpkits - this unlocks every character their customization options
unlockallmpcards - this gives you every item at level 1, including a power reset card if you don't have one. Unfortunately you can't use this 10 times to get everything but it saves you having to get one roll of most items
grantmpcredits ## - this gives you the specified amount of credits that you can then spend in store

Buy recruit packs until you have all the level 10 common weapons, then veteran packs until you have all the level 10 uncommon weapons, and finally arsenal packs until you have all the level 10 ultra rare weapons. If you don't use the console to unlock the characters then you should buy reserves packs until you have all of the characters and then arsenal packs. All of the 99k packs have the same chance to give you a UR weapon but arsenal packs cannot give characters so you get more level 4 consumable items by buying them.

If you still want to grind then here's the average amount of credits required to reach a certain baseline of equipment. Each tier assumes you opened packs optimally to reach that tier, so getting all level 10 rare weapons includes getting all level 10 common and uncommon weapons:

[olist]
 [*] 1 million credits for all level 10 common weapons
 [*] 5 million credits for all level 10 uncommon weapons
 [*] 20 million credits for all level 10 rare  weapons
 [*] 50 million credits for all level 10 rare weapons, all level 5 attachments, and all level 5 gear mods
 [*] 150 million credits for all level 10 ultra rare weapons
[/olist]

There is one very good reason to purchase this game despite the legacy edition - multiplayer. People still log on to play some 4-person horde-mode, 10 phase challenges. It is still possible to get achievements, and the store is still available to upgrade armor, ammo, and obtain new characters. 

I log on when I feel the need to shoot reaper, collector, cerberus, or geth forces. It is pretty fun... and depending on your skill or character or gear, it is possible to solo the hordes.

Mass Effect 3 (2012) with all DLCs is a powerful, satisfying finale to Shepard’s story. It delivers on emotion, scale, and big sci-fi moments while giving players a real sense that their choices mattered across the entire trilogy.

Combat feels tight and responsive, with refined abilities and solid squad play that make battles more tactical and exciting. The multiplayer is a very nice bonus for replayability and helps you unlock gear that matters in single player without feeling forced. Still available in 2025 after 13 years!

The achievements weren't too hard or tedious, most of you probably remember legendary edition's achievements, the only one I've spent like 2 3 hours of grinding was Veteran "kill 5k enemies".

Where the game really shines is in the characters and the emotional stakes. Old faces return, new ones leave an impression, and the conversations hit hard when they need to. The DLC content adds meaningful layers to the universe - extra missions, deeper lore, and a few personal payoffs that enrich the main campaign, and add in a couple of laughs and time offs that really feel needed.

The soundtrack, visuals, and set pieces sell the scale of the conflict. Big moments land, quiet moments breathe, and the ending feels earned if you’ve invested in the story and your crew.

If you’re looking for an intense, emotional sci-fi RPG that ties together a massive story and rewards player investment, Mass Effect 3 with all DLCs is well worth playing. It left me satisfied, moved, and ready to revisit the trilogy again.

I always say I would definitely recommend the Mass Effect universe to anyone. It has the deepest emotional wiring out of most story games.
